sample.question: What ordering does a queue follow, and what do enqueue and dequeue do?
sample.answer: A queue follows first in, first out (FIFO) ordering: enqueue adds an item at the rear, and dequeue removes the oldest item from the front.
sample.sourceQuote: A queue follows first in, first out (FIFO) ordering.

sample.question: How does a stack differ from a queue in its ordering?
sample.answer: A stack follows last in, first out (LIFO) ordering, so pop removes the most recently added item.
sample.sourceQuote: A stack instead follows last in, first out (LIFO) ordering.

sample.question: What happens when you enqueue to a full Aster queue or dequeue from an empty one?
sample.answer: When full, enqueue rejects the new item and preserves all existing items; when empty, dequeue returns the sentinel EMPTY.
sample.sourceQuote: When the Aster queue is full, enqueue rejects the new item and preserves all existing items.

sample.question: What ordering rule does a queue follow?
sample.explanation: The document states that a queue follows first in, first out (FIFO) ordering, so the oldest item is removed first. Last in, first out describes a stack, not a queue.
sample.sourceQuote: A queue follows first in, first out (FIFO) ordering.

sample.question: Why does the circular buffer implementation also store a count of occupied slots?
options: It allows the buffer to grow beyond its fixed capacity
It speeds up searching for an arbitrary item to O(1)
It makes the head index point to the newest item
It removes ambiguity when head and tail have the same value
sample.correctAnswer: It removes ambiguity when head and tail have the same value
sample.explanation: In a circular buffer, head and tail can hold the same index value whether the buffer is empty or full, so the stored count distinguishes those states. The count does not affect search speed or capacity, and the head still points to the oldest item.
sample.sourceQuote: The count removes ambiguity when head and tail have the same value.
